text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for single-tenant customer `Starlane` on dedicated pool starlane-prod-1. Current p99 = 2.1s (SLO 1.2s). Paging on-call.
alyssa_oncall: Acked. Pulling graphs now. @ben_sre can you join? :phone:
ben_sre: On it. I'm seeing clustered p99 jumps aligned with a burst of streaming connections at 14:02 UTC. p95 mildly elevated too. Looks like streaming stalls and tail spikes.
arnav_infra: Correlating with node metrics — GPU utilization ~95% on a few workers, CPU OK. Network egress per-host spiked. Could be KV cache thrash or large prefix eviction.
jia_ml: Noted an unusual prompt pattern from Starlane yesterday — extremely long system prompts and repeated context refreshes. Could cause K/V growth. Any sample prompts from support? @dana_support
support-dana: I have a few anonymized logs from the customer session. Pasting examples:
```
USER_PROMPT: "Summarize the following policy document: [very long blob ~120k chars]" x3 in rapid succession
SESSION: 80 concurrent streaming sessions from same tenant
```
luca_starlane: We're running a new feature that streams multi-chunk documents. We saw an increased Beta user cohort concurrently hitting the summarize API at 14:00 UTC. We're investigating if our client is re-sending on timeouts.
alyssa_oncall: Immediate mitigation options?
ben_sre: Short-term: 1) enable model fallback to lower-memory variant for Starlane route, 2) enable streaming fallback mode (non-KV) to avoid repeated KV cache growth, 3) throttle per-tenant concurrency at edge.
arnav_infra: I can flip the route to fallback model and enable a conservative concurrency cap in the router for that tenant. Commands:
```
# route to smaller model variant
redwoodctl route update --tenant starlane --model redwood-medium-quant
# set tenant concurrency cap
redwoodctl quota set --tenant starlane --max-streams 40
```
ben_sre: I'll also push an emergency autoscaler policy to treat this pool as burstable so additional workers can be provisioned sooner.
jia_ml: ML note: quantized model variant may increase token latency slightly but lowers memory pressure a lot and avoids KV thrash. Good short-term tradeoff.
dana_support: Notifying Starlane that we're investigating and applying mitigations. Draft: "We're seeing a high-volume summarization burst; applying routing changes to stabilize latency. Will follow up with timeline." @luca_starlane ok to send?
luca_starlane: Please send. We're already throttling client retries on our side.
alyssa_oncall: Plan: apply route fallback + concurrency cap (arnav), enable autoscaler adjustment (ben), monitor metrics and streaming error rates (jia). If stable in 10m, re-evaluate rollback to normal path.
arnav_infra: Applying route update now.
```
[deploy-bot] 14:06 UTC: route update accepted for tenant starlane -> redwood-medium-quant
```
ben_sre: Pushing autoscaler tweak.
```
# emergency pod burst policy
kubectl patch hpa starlane-pool -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":12}}'
```
jia_ml: Watching p99 and streaming stall rate. Initial signal: p99 dropped to 1.6s after route switch but streaming stall errors rose (clients seeing EPIPE / truncated streams).
alyssa_oncall: Are those client-side retries causing duplicate sessions? dana, any evidence?
dana_support: Logs show multiple session restarts from same session id within few seconds. Might be client retry policy + stream truncation.
ben_sre: Let's enable streaming fallback 'chunked-ack' mode which avoids long-lived KV caching and uses server-side checkpointing. Enabling now for tenant.
arnav_infra: Done. `redwoodctl streaming update --tenant starlane --mode chunked-ack`
```
[observability-bot] 14:12 UTC: p99=1.05s, p95=0.42s, streaming_error_rate=0.8% (was 4.1%)
```
jia_ml: Good signal. Still see two nodes with high GPU memory churn - likely from largest open sessions. Might need to evict longest-affinity sessions.
alyssa_oncall: Action: schedule soft-eviction for sessions older than 2m on that pool. ben, can you do graceful eviction?
ben_sre: Kicking eviction script:
```
python tools/evict_long_sessions.py --pool starlane-prod-1 --age 120
```
alyssa_oncall: Post-eviction numbers?
```
[observability-bot] 14:18 UTC: p99=0.95s, streaming_error_rate=0.6%, GPU_mem_pressure nodes=1
```
alyssa_oncall: Looks stable. I'm going to hand off to day SRE for follow-up and postmortem. @ben_sre please own follow-up; @jia_ml please add ML-runbook notes about long-prompt handling and quantization guidance.
ben_sre: Will take it. I'll gather traces, slow request samples, and client logs for RCA. Initial hypothesis: client-driven prompt storm + KV cache mutation + concurrency spike.
jia_ml: I'll add a rule to the model router to prefer non-KV paths for >60k char prompts or when session length > X.
dana_support: Customer update sent at 14:25 UTC: "We've applied routing/backoff to stabilize. We'll provide a timeline and recommendations shortly."
luca_starlane: Thanks team. We'll throttle our client and share more logs.
alyssa_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated. P95/P99 back within SLOs. Opening an incident ticket and assigning postmortem tasks.
incident-bot: INCIDENT #2026-1755554321 MITIGATED -> Owner: ben_sre, Severity: Sev2, Follow-up: collect traces, add router rule, docs for customers on streaming best-practices.
ben_sre: I'll include recommended client-side changes for Starlane: exponential backoff, per-session rate limit, avoid re-sends on transient truncation. Also schedule a meeting with their eng team if needed.
jia_ml: Adding an ML runbook PR to repo: `docs/runbooks/long-prefix-handling.md` with quantization and streaming fallback guidance.
alyssa_oncall: Thanks everyone. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
